scenarios.title: The root cause now looks obvious
scenarios.prompt: After an outage, the failed component is easy to identify. Reviewers say the on-call engineer should have known immediately, although several alerts looked equally plausible during the incident.
scenarios.question: What should the review reconstruct first?

options.text: The timeline of information available at each decision point, before the root cause was known.
The final root-cause diagram, because it contains the complete truth.
Which engineer now gives the most confident explanation.

scenarios.explanation: Hindsight compresses uncertainty after the outcome. A contemporaneous decision record restores what was knowable and which alternatives were reasonable at the time.
missingEvidence: The alerts visible at each time.
Actions available under the actual time pressure.
scenarios.evidenceNote: Hindsight bias is a useful lens for the review language, but the reconstruction may still reveal preventable process failures.
scenarios.nextAction: Build an evidence timeline before judging the quality of incident decisions.

scenarios.title: One outage creates a permanent rule
scenarios.prompt: A rare database failure causes a severe outage. The team proposes an expensive control for every system without checking how often the failure occurs or whether the control addresses other risks.
scenarios.question: What should happen before the control becomes policy?

options.text: Define the evidence and recurrence threshold that would justify the control across systems.
Approve it quickly because severe incidents should always produce broad rules.
Wait until the incident feels less memorable, then use intuition again.

scenarios.explanation: The vivid outage can dominate risk judgment. Predefined criteria make the policy depend on recurrence, exposure and control effectiveness rather than memory alone.
missingEvidence: Base rate of the failure mode.
Expected risk reduction and operating cost of the control.
scenarios.evidenceNote: Availability is a plausible risk because one severe event dominates the proposal. A rare event can still justify a broad control when expected harm is high.
scenarios.nextAction: Set a measurable adoption rule and test it against the system portfolio.
